- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods after spike.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3+ consecutive periods, apply mean reversion: cap forecast at 1.5–2σ above recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits short-term noise; use 10-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
- If true outcome is below model by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, assume “bearish sentiment bias” — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next period.
- If sentiment history shows rapid shift from negative to positive, model often fails to adjust quickly — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods.
